meta.description: Detects allele-specific transcription factor or histone modification binding from heterozygous-variant ChIP-seq using WASP, RASQUAL, BaalChIP with measured RAF or gDNA correction, and an explicitly external-only AlleleSeq route.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output fabricates study identifiers, sample sizes, p-values, efficacy data, or live execution. Public and synthetic fixtures are labeled, and unavailable BaalChIP model and AlleleSeq full-toolchain execution receive no credit.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill remains a research-analysis workflow, makes no patient-specific diagnosis or treatment recommendation, and keeps prediction, within-sample ASB, and population QTL interpretations distinct.

methodological_ground.detail: Mapping bias, imprinting, chrX, allele dose, replicate depth, convergence, multiplicity, and correction-source provenance are handled explicitly. Versioned method claims are bound to their exact sources and runtime contracts.

code_usability.detail: All accessible code parsed and executed: R contracts and version gates, Python tests, RAF and gDNA preflights, ten negative boundaries, cleanup, paired WASP and provider HDF5, interval controls, and a two-feature public RASQUAL cohort. Resource-infeasible or unavailable surfaces remain uncredited.

functional_suitability.note: The four advertised routes, confounders, outputs, and scientific boundaries are covered with coherent exact bindings; the BaalChIP statistical model is not runnable in the bounded prepared environment.

reliability.note: Accessible runners fail closed, refuse output reuse, preserve atomicity, and expose structured errors. Full BaalChIP terminal publication remains resource-infeasible and therefore unverified.

performance_context.note: Progressive disclosure and bounded runners are efficient; the legacy AlleleSeq and compiled Bioconductor surfaces necessarily carry substantial dependency cost.

agent_usability.note: Routing, preflights, stop conditions, version gates, output contracts, failure classifications, and interpretation guidance are explicit and coherent.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers, method selection, prerequisite lists, command surfaces, and troubleshooting boundaries make the skill discoverable without weakening scientific validation.

security.note: No credentials, raw-code evaluation, user-command shell interpolation, broad deletion, or private-data retention appears; schemas and paths are validated before execution.

maintainability.note: Documentation, contracts, model runner, cohort driver, and focused tests are cleanly separated; a live BaalChIP integration regression awaits a prepared compiled dependency stack.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, progressive disclosure, composable file contracts, idempotent output refusal, exact source identities, and explicit external routing are strong.

inputs.label: Paired-end WASP mapping-bias route
inputs.note: Fresh v0.3.4 paired execution and provider HDF5 construction passed filenames, shapes, pairing, and stage-count invariants.

assertions.text: The paired remap command consumes the exact fq1 and fq2 files emitted by WASP v0.3.4.
assertions.note: Fresh output names were input.remap.fq1.gz and input.remap.fq2.gz, and both contained six records.

assertions.text: Every final WASP alignment remains paired.
assertions.note: All four final alignments carried the paired flag.

assertions.text: Final alignments equal direct keeps plus remap keeps and do not exceed input alignments.
assertions.note: The fresh run satisfied final=4, direct+remap=4, and input=4.

assertions.text: The provider chromosome-22 IMPUTE2 and haplotype inputs produce the expected HDF5 shapes.
assertions.note: All four expected /chr22 shapes were independently inspected and matched.

assertions.text: The workflow reports observed attrition rather than assuming a fixed percentage.
assertions.note: The documentation requires input, remap, retained, tested, and significant counts.

inputs.label: Cancer BaalChIP workflow with RAF or gDNA correction
inputs.note: Every accessible contract, preflight, error boundary, version gate, and cleanup behavior passed; the model and terminal publications remain resource-infeasible and uncredited.

assertions.text: RAF mode requires measured RAF and refuses ordinary AF.
assertions.note: Measured RAF preflight passed and AF substitution stopped with [missing_raf].

assertions.text: gDNA mode records the indexed BAM actually used for correction.
assertions.note: The fresh correction-provenance file names the indexed gDNA BAM and records a matching chr contig style.

assertions.text: Invalid schema, assembly, contig, sample, interval, file, correction, and output states fail closed.
assertions.note: Ten independent negative probes returned the expected structured error codes.

assertions.text: A package-load failure removes only the owned staging directory and publishes no final result.
assertions.note: The missing-package run exited nonzero, left no final or matching partial, and preserved an unrelated sentinel.

assertions.text: The documented release, runtime gate, and used source interfaces form one reproducible BaalChIP contract.
assertions.note: Official metadata and source bind BaalChIP 1.36.0 to Bioconductor 3.22 and R 4.5; candidate constants, status, tests, and used APIs match.

inputs.label: Imprinting, blacklist, chrX, and contract boundaries
inputs.note: Live interval controls and focused helper tests passed, including report-list shape, structured empty schema, assembly rejection, and exclusion boundaries.

assertions.text: Imprinted-locus exclusion retains the expected two of three rows.
assertions.note: The live bedtools control retained the non-overlapping chr1 and chrX rows.

assertions.text: Autosomal filtering removes chrX and retains two rows.
assertions.note: The live awk control produced two autosomal rows and no chrX row.

assertions.text: Assembly and contig-style mismatches are rejected before model execution.
assertions.note: Fresh probes stopped with [assembly_mismatch] and [contig_mismatch].

assertions.text: The group report contract selects a named data frame and supports a structured empty result.
assertions.note: The base-R helper suite passed named-list, required-column, empty-report, and incompatible-report cases.

assertions.text: Imprinting and X-linked skew are not overinterpreted as ordinary differential binding.
assertions.note: The skill consistently requires filtering or separate labeling and an X-aware interpretation.

inputs.label: Public two-feature RASQUAL cohort
inputs.note: The candidate prepared exact binary matrices and ran both public chr11 features once, with convergence, phi, p-value, cohort BH, and overwrite assertions.

assertions.text: The prepare command validates matrix dimensions and emits exact native-double byte counts.
assertions.note: Fresh binaries represented two features by 24 samples and 24 samples by four covariates at eight bytes per value.

assertions.text: Every manifest feature executes exactly once.
assertions.note: C11orf21 and TSPAN32 each appeared once in the two-row result family.

assertions.text: Every emitted row satisfies the 25-column RASQUAL contract with finite phi and convergence zero.
assertions.note: Both public rows passed all three checks.

assertions.text: The wrapper derives finite raw p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg q-values across the emitted cohort family.
assertions.note: Both appended p and cohort q fields were finite and within [0,1].

assertions.text: A repeated cohort run refuses to overwrite the existing output.
assertions.note: The repeated command exited two with the candidate-level refusing-to-overwrite error.

inputs.label: AlleleSeq personalized-genome routing boundary
inputs.note: The exact tested implementation is bound separately from the canonical method citation and the unavailable legacy stack remains external-only and uncredited.

assertions.text: The skill does not advertise an incomplete local AlleleSeq execution as a success.
assertions.note: The route is explicitly external-only and the fresh probe records an unavailable full toolchain.

assertions.text: The required legacy prerequisites are named precisely.
assertions.note: Python 2, STAR, Picard, Java, Make, reference and liftOver resources, and the official vcf2diploid JAR are listed.

assertions.text: No unofficial vcf2diploid substitute is used.
assertions.note: No JAR was present or substituted, and no personalized-genome result was claimed.

assertions.text: The tested implementation is bound to its exact repository and commit.
assertions.note: The read-only checkout reports https://github.com/trgaleev/AlleleSeq2.git at cfe8acf88989922da841e71238b360f8f57e813a, matching the candidate.

assertions.text: The canonical method paper is retained separately from implementation provenance.
assertions.note: The candidate identifies Rozowsky et al. as the canonical method and trgaleev/AlleleSeq2 as the tested implementation.

key_strengths: The paired WASP route matches the pinned provider filenames and preserves explicit fragment-count, pairing, and provider-HDF5 invariants.
The RASQUAL driver validates binary dimensions, exact feature coverage, strict output shape, convergence, finite phi, and family-level BH correction.
The BaalChIP route binds one official 1.36.0/3.22/R4.5 contract, validates correction provenance, fails closed, and cleans only owned staging state.
Unavailable BaalChIP model and AlleleSeq legacy components are classified honestly and receive no inferred execution credit.
Claim-level provenance separates canonical scientific methods from exact tested implementations.
